title: Champagne Emoji 🍾 Meaning: Pop the Bottle, It’s a Party
description: 🍾 is the champagne emoji: a bottle with its cork flying. It means big celebrations, New Year's Eve, wins and launches. See its uses and its occasional innuendo.
summary: The 🍾 bottle with popping cork emoji, widely called the champagne emoji, means a major celebration is underway. It marks New Year's Eve, victories, weddings, launches and big announcements. It expresses louder, more exuberant excitement than a toast, and is occasionally used as sexual innuendo.
meaning: The cork leaving a champagne bottle is the sound of something being achieved, and 🍾 puts that burst into a message. It is used at the moment of success: the offer signed, the exam passed, the championship won, the clock striking midnight. Compared with clinking glasses, it is less about polite congratulation and more about release. A row of bottles reads like a room erupting.

Certain scenes are built around it. Winning athletes spray champagne on podiums and in locker rooms, so sports fans post 🍾 after titles. Nightlife culture has “bottle service” and “popping bottles,” phrases repeated in countless songs, which gives the emoji a club-and-VIP flavor. Startups use it for funding news and product launches. And New Year's Eve, bachelorette parties and weddings account for an enormous share of everyday use.

It can be anticipatory as well: “if this goes through, 🍾” puts the bottle on ice. People also use it for small victories with deliberate exaggeration, like finishing a tax return. In sexual contexts the image of a bottle erupting can stand for ejaculation, usually next to 🍆 or 💦, but this is far rarer than the celebratory meaning and needs an unmistakably explicit setup.

contexts.label: In texting
contexts.body: It is the exclamation mark of good news. Friends fire it back when someone shares a win, often several at once. It announces plans to go out and celebrate properly. Used for trivial accomplishments, such as finally doing the laundry, it becomes a joke about treating oneself to applause.

contexts.label: On holidays and at events
contexts.body: December 31 is the high point, with countdown posts and party photos. Engagements, weddings and milestone birthdays follow. Bachelorette parties pair it with a ring and a veil. It also shows up for graduations and retirements, anywhere a real bottle might be opened.

contexts.label: In sports and business
contexts.body: Championship wins, promotions to a higher league and race victories bring it out among fans. In business, it marks acquisitions, launches, record quarters and funding announcements, especially on LinkedIn and X. In both worlds it says the result is worth a real celebration, not just a nod.

examples.text: Signed the lease on the new studio today 🍾
examples.meaning: Announcing a business or personal milestone.
Counting down to midnight on New Year's Eve.

examples.text: If I pass the bar exam, we're popping 🍾
examples.meaning: Promising a celebration if a hoped-for result comes through.

examples.text: Inbox zero for the first time since 2019 🍾

combos.meaning: Opening champagne and toasting; a full celebration.
Celebrating a title or major win.

confusedWith.difference: 🥂 is the graceful toast, suitable for formal congratulations. 🍾 is the noisy opening of the bottle and conveys more energy and excitement. Many messages use both in sequence.
🎉 is the all-purpose celebration emoji with no alcohol involved. 🍾 implies a bigger, more adult occasion and a real drink being poured.
🍶 is a Japanese sake flask and cup. It is a bottle of alcohol too, but it signals Japanese dining and quiet drinking, not Western-style celebration.

avoid: Avoid celebrating with it in front of people affected badly by the same news, such as colleagues who lost out.
Don't use it around people in recovery or for events involving children.
Skip pairing it with sexual emojis unless the innuendo is intended and welcome.
design: A dark green champagne bottle with gold foil at the neck is shown tilted, its cork shooting out with a spray of foam or bubbles. Labels differ in color and shape among vendors, and some add motion lines or sparkles. The flying cork is depicted on all major platforms and is the defining element.

faqs.q: What does 🍾 mean from a guy or girl?
faqs.a: They are celebrating or think you should be. It typically follows good news or precedes a night out. In a sexually explicit conversation it could be innuendo, but in normal use it only means a party or a win.

The bottle is the pop; the glasses are the toast. 🍾 shows excitement and the start of festivities, while 🥂 expresses congratulations and good wishes. For a restrained or professional message, the glasses are the gentler option.

Occasionally. The erupting bottle can represent ejaculation in explicit exchanges, usually together with other suggestive emojis. This is uncommon. Without that context, people will read it as plain celebration.

The design is a champagne-style bottle, but people use it for any sparkling wine and for celebration in general. It often appears where no bottle exists at all, as a way of saying “this deserves a party.”

faqs.q: When was the champagne emoji added?
faqs.a: It was released in 2015 with Emoji 1.0, giving people a dedicated celebration bottle one year before the clinking champagne glasses arrived.
